svg.title: serial-broker at a glance
svg.desc: What serial-broker does for web applications that use a serial device from several browser tabs, how it fits between an application, the browser and the devices, and which problem each of its features solves.
svg.text: Web Serial for applications that run in several tabs: shared, handed over, reconnected, with no coordination code.

g.text: ✕ Only one tab can open the port
✕ That tab closes: the device is gone for all
✕ Device unplugged: dead until someone reloads
✓ Every tab reads from and writes to the device
✓ That tab closes or crashes: another takes over
✓ Device comes back: so does the connection
Everything runs in the browser, on your origin. No server component, no browser extension.
Browser · your origin · HTTPS or localhost
exactly one tab holds a port
One configuration per device, as many as you need
Any framework or none. ESM, CommonJS and
The worker script. Most bundlers emit it;
Your logger, a diagnostics API, and a
ready-made debugging page to deploy or not.
Whatever you need, it is there
The problems a serial device shared by several tabs runs into, and what serial-broker does about each.
Several tabs need the same device
One port for every tab: all of them read
and write, and no write is sent twice.
The tab holding the port closes
Another tab takes over, even after a crash,
The device is unplugged or turned off
The port reopens with the same settings,
at once when the device reappears.
Writes not yet begun go out once; a begun
one is reported, never silently repeated.
Scale, printer and reader at once
A text protocol, or binary frames
Bytes pass through untouched; text is
Users should choose the port once
The configuration is remembered and the
browser keeps the permission: no prompt.
strict CSP, a worker script not deployed.

that says what to do about it.
Structured logs, a diagnostics API, and a
